name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of combined deficiency of multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of multisystem clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial disease including neurological and muscular symptoms
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Combined biochemical evidence of multiple respiratory chain complex deficiencies plus compatible clinical features and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and biochemical assays remain important for diagnosis when genetic testing is inconclusive.

searchTerms: fatigue and muscle weakness on activity

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions or cerebral atrophy
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and muscle atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial respiratory chain complex subunits or assembly factors (e.g., SURF1, SCO2, or others)
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers
Abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent stroke-like lesions on MRI
Isolated optic neuropathy without multisystem involvement
Typically adolescent or young adult onset

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with multisystem involvement
Persistent lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Early onset cardiomyopathy with neurological symptoms
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
